Some modbus devices have spontaneous fluxes and deliver an error when being read, next time it is ok again. This behaviour ruins any statistics.

Lazy_error_count tells the integration to ignore a number of errors (pr entity) before setting the entity to unavailable.

issue_context.title: Modbus: Busy Slave is *still* recored als 0 (Zero)
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Same as here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/51103#issuecomment-860573695

If this happens:
```
2021-08-08 15:43:22 ERROR (SyncWorker_3) [homeassistant.components.modbus.modbus] Pymodbus: Exception Response(131, 3, SlaveBusy)
2021-08-08 15:43:38 ERROR (SyncWorker_4) [homeassistant.components.modbus.modbus] Pymodbus: Exception Response(131, 3, SlaveBusy)
```

...this happens:
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5020623/128756349-248fe8c5-bfb2-4ad0-af27-773f1127fbd1.png)

Old issue was closed before I had the chance to test it. Now still popping up in the current release.

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.8.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2021.4x (could be 2021.3.x)

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Modbus

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/modbus/

### Example YAML snippet


comments:
Hey there @adamchengtkc, @janiversen, @vzahradnik, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`modbus`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L311) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

But that is not an error, if your device reports an error (busy in this case) the integration sets the sensor to unaviable. This of course affect your curves. You can always use automation to do something with the raw values, but the integration only reports what it receives.

I’m not sure that is the case. 

If a sensor is unavailable it says exactly this and the line in the graph drops out. In this case, either the Modbus integration apparently interprets the error as 0 or the device is delivering a 0 instead of a value when it’s busy. 

What does the integration do if the slave reports busy? Shouldn’t it report the sensor as unavailable instead of 0 (regardless what the fail value of the device is)?

I could of course run this through a filter - if you believe the bug is with the modbus device I will do that.

Let´s have a look at the code:

Your device sends the an exception message "slave busy" (see log), this is caught at modbus communication level (modbus.py line 310-319):
```
try:
            result = entry.func(address, value, **kwargs)
        except ModbusException as exception_error:
            self._log_error(str(exception_error))
            return None
        if not hasattr(result, entry.attr):
            self._log_error(str(result))
            return None
        self._in_error = False
        return result
```
An exception message do not have attributes so we log the error, and return None to the entity layer (sensor.py line 63-73):
```
        result = await self._hub.async_pymodbus_call(
            self._slave, self._address, self._count, self._input_type
        )
        if result is None:
            self._attr_available = False
            self.async_write_ha_state()
            return

        self._attr_state = self.unpack_structure_result(result.registers)
        self._attr_available = True
        self.async_write_ha_state()
```
In case of "None" the entity is set unavailable, but the value is not touched.

If you see anything wrong please let me know and I will make a PR right away.

there is a rather tight test harness, where e.g. message exceptions are tested, but currently I do not control what happens to the value, I will add that test later today, and add you as reviewer, that might be the best way to see what is going on.

what I could do is implement an "error_counter" and instead of reporting the error immediately, suppress the error until it has occurred e.g. 10 times. That would work as a filter for spontaneous errors.

Hi @janiversen and thanks for the quick reply!

> ...I will add that test later today, and add you as reviewer, that might be the best way to see what is going on.

Not sure if I can be of any help as I am not a developer and don't have the environment to run test builds. :( I can however deploy betas to a VM test system.

> what I could do is implement an "error_counter" and instead of reporting the error immediately, suppress the error until it has occurred e.g. 10 times. That would work as a filter for spontaneous errors.

I think that would be great - typically the refresh is every 30sec, so after 10 times (5min down) I'd say it would be reasonable to throw an exception. From what I can tell Modbus is a bit picky for paralle requests - the way you describe it should solve the problem as failures are probably spread over different registers and it wouldn't be an issue if a sensor update will happen seconds to minutes later.

review_comments: Do we need a config option? Maybe just use a sane default?

"need" is defined be the user 😄 In many situations especially when trying to locate an error (in the hardware etc), it is good to have "lazy_error: 0".

While in production, you most times do not really care if you miss 2-3 measurements, but having a nasty 0 in your graph is disturbing, in that case it is good to have "lazy_error: 3".

So I think a parameter is needed.

I think there's two problem areas and both have better solutions. If there's a problem with the device reading I'd adjust the reading and if there's a problem with the how the graph draws the accumulated data points I'd adjust the data vizualization.

But ok.
